units.title: Physical Chemistry
topics: Chemical arithmetic: Dalton's theory, laws of stoichiometry, atomic and molecular mass, empirical and molecular formula, limiting reactant, Avogadro's hypothesis, equivalent masses
States of matter: gaseous, liquid and solid states
Atomic structure and periodic classification of elements
Ionic equilibrium, acid, base and salt
Energetics of chemical reactions, chemical kinetics, chemical bonding and shape of molecules

sections.title: Ionic equilibrium, acid, base and salt

summary: Convert everything to moles first; the limiting reagent decides the yield.
Quantum numbers fix orbitals: 2l+1 per subshell; cations lose 4s before 3d.
Count oxidation-number change to find n-factor and equivalent mass.
For acid–base mixtures find the excess; weak acids use √KaC; buffers use Henderson.
One faraday = one equivalent; E^°cell is cathode minus anode.
Order is read from the rate law, not the equation; first-order half-life is constant.
Shape comes from electron pairs including lone pairs.

units.title: Inorganic Chemistry
topics: Non-metals: hydrogen, oxygen, ozone, water, nitrogen and its compounds, halogens, carbon, phosphorus, sulphur, noble gases and environmental pollution
Metals: metallurgical principles, alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, coinage metals (copper, silver, gold)
Extraction of metals: zinc, mercury, and iron compounds

sections.title: Extraction of metals: zinc, mercury, iron compounds

summary: Each industrial process has one catalyst: Fe (Haber), Pt (Ostwald), V₂O₅ (Contact).
Know the oxidation products of copper with dilute versus concentrated nitric acid.
Roast sulphides, calcine carbonates, smelt oxides; slag is CaSiO₃.
Group 2 carbonates and sulphates become more stable / less soluble down the group.
SO₂ and NOₓ give acid rain; CFCs destroy ozone; CO₂ and CH₄ warm the planet.

units.title: Organic Chemistry
topics: Introduction: fundamental principles, purification, nomenclature, structural isomerism, idea of reaction mechanism
Hydrocarbons: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatic hydrocarbons
Aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and derivatives
Nitro compounds and amines, aromatic and aliphatic

sections.title: Introduction: principles, purification, nomenclature, isomerism, mechanism
Aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and derivatives

summary: Name by the principal group; count isomers carefully (C₅H₁₂ has 3).
Markovnikov for HX; peroxide reverses HBr; ozonolysis cuts at C=C.
SN1 follows carbocation stability; SN2 follows steric access.
Only carbonyls with α-H do aldol; only those without do Cannizzaro.
Lucas distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols; iodoform needs CH₃CH(OH)– or CH₃CO–.
Diazotise aniline at 0–5 °C; then Sandmeyer or couple.
